# Toggle Button

A button that stays on: an on/off state the user sets directly, announced with aria-pressed.

```tsx
import { ToggleButton } from "@rata/react";
```

| | |
|---|---|
| Registry name | `toggle-button` |
| Family | buttons |
| Tier | free |
| Status (css / react / figma) | latest / latest / future |
| Depends on | `button`, `state-layer`, `spinner` |

## Behavior

Pressed-state semantics over the button's own activation contract. State is not held here: the caller owns `pressed` and is told what it should become, which is what lets a toggle inside a group and a toggle on its own be the same primitive.

Headless contract: `getToggleButtonProps` in `packages/primitives/src/toggle-button.ts` — importable from `@rata/primitives` without the React wrapper or any CSS.

- **Composes `getButtonProps` instead of reimplementing activation** — A toggle is a button that carries a state. Implementing the disabled and loading guards a second time is how the two drift apart — one gains a fix the other doesn't, and the difference only shows up in whichever one nobody tested.
- **`aria-pressed` is emitted in both states, never omitted when false** — Unlike `aria-disabled`, which is absent when it doesn't apply, a missing `aria-pressed` makes the control announce as an ordinary button — precisely when the user most needs to know it is a toggle that is currently off.
- **`aria-pressed`, not `role="switch"`** — A switch is an on/off setting that takes effect immediately and reads as a thing with a state ("Notifications, on"). A toggle button is an action you leave engaged — bold, mute, pin — and reads as a verb. When the control is a setting, the answer is Switch, and this component is the wrong one.
- **The label does not change with the state** — `aria-pressed` already says whether it is on. Swapping the label to "Unmute" as well means the name and the state contradict each other — a screen reader announces "Unmute, pressed", which is a double negative the user has to unpick. The visual treatment carries the state; the word stays put.
- **No `data-pressed` attribute** — `[aria-pressed="true"]` is already a CSS selector. A parallel data attribute would be a second copy of the same fact, free to go stale.
- **Controlled by default, with an uncontrolled escape hatch** — A toggle almost always reflects state that lives somewhere else — a document's formatting, a saved preference — so the controlled form is the honest default. `defaultPressed` exists for the genuinely local case, and passing both is a conflict rather than a precedence rule to memorize.

## Props

Extends `Omit<ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>, "disabled" | "onChange">`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pressed?` | `boolean` | — | Whether the toggle is currently on. Makes the component controlled. |
| `defaultPressed?` | `boolean` | — | Starting state for an uncontrolled toggle that owns its own value. |
| `onPressedChange?` | `(pressed: boolean, event: MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => void` | — | Called with the state the toggle should move to — not the one it is leaving. |
| `variant?` | `ToggleButtonVariant` | `"secondary"` | How loud the toggle is in its off state. |
| `size?` | `ToggleButtonSize` | `"md"` | Control height and inline padding, from the `size.control.*` scale. Text size does not change with it. |
| `disabled?` | `boolean` | — | Blocks activation while keeping the toggle focusable, announced, and readable in its current state. |
| `loading?` | `boolean` | — | Shows a spinner and refuses activation while the change this toggle asked for is still in flight. |
| `iconOnly?` | `boolean` | — | Square toggle carrying an icon and no visible text. |

### `pressed`

```ts
pressed?: boolean
```

Whether the toggle is currently on. Makes the component controlled.

**Use when**

- Whenever the state lives outside the component — which is nearly always, since a toggle usually reflects something a document or a preference already knows.

**Don't use for**

- Passing it without `onPressedChange`; the toggle would render its state and then refuse to ever change it.
- Deriving it from the last click rather than from the thing being toggled — if the underlying change fails, the button is left lying about it.

**Conflicts with** `defaultPressed`

**Accessibility** Becomes `aria-pressed`, emitted in both states. This is the only thing that tells assistive technology the control is a toggle at all.

### `defaultPressed`

```ts
defaultPressed?: boolean
```

Starting state for an uncontrolled toggle that owns its own value.

Source doc: Starting state for an uncontrolled toggle. Conflicts with `pressed`.

**Use when**

- Genuinely local state nothing else reads — a disclosure of extra columns in one table, say.

**Don't use for**

- Anything the rest of the page reacts to. The moment two places need the value, uncontrolled means they disagree.
- Resetting the toggle by changing this later — it is read once, at mount.

**Conflicts with** `pressed`

**Accessibility** No difference in what is announced: `aria-pressed` is emitted either way.

### `onPressedChange`

```ts
onPressedChange?: (pressed: boolean, event: MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => void
```

Called with the state the toggle should move to — not the one it is leaving.

Source doc: Called with the state the toggle should move to, not the one it is in.

**Use when**

- Applying the change, then letting the new state flow back in through `pressed`.

**Don't use for**

- Reading the current value off the event target; the argument already says where it is going.
- Treating it as a plain click handler — it does not fire when the toggle is disabled or loading.

**Accessibility** Fires for keyboard activation too, since it hangs off the same click guard the button uses. Space and Enter behave as they do on any native button.

### `variant`

```ts
variant?: ToggleButtonVariant = "secondary"
```

How loud the toggle is in its off state.

**Use when**

- `tertiary` for a toolbar of many toggles, where a border each would be visual noise.
- `secondary` for one or two toggles that need to read as controls on their own.

**Don't use for**

- Expecting a `primary` or `destructive` toggle. A filled accent control reads as "the action to take", which fights with "a state you are in", and a destructive thing you can leave switched on is a bug waiting to happen.

**Accessibility** Visual only. The pressed state must never be carried by colour alone — the on state changes fill *and* is announced through `aria-pressed`.

### `size`

```ts
size?: ToggleButtonSize = "md"
```

Control height and inline padding, from the `size.control.*` scale. Text size does not change with it.

**Use when**

- Matching the density of the surrounding controls, exactly as `Button` does — including that the label stays one size across all three.

**Don't use for**

- Mixing sizes within one group of toggles — they read as a set, so they measure as a set.
- Expecting an icon-only toggle's glyph to grow with it. The glyph follows the text size, which is constant, so only the box changes.

### `disabled`

```ts
disabled?: boolean
```

Blocks activation while keeping the toggle focusable, announced, and readable in its current state.

**Use when**

- A toggle that cannot change yet but whose current state still matters to see.

**Don't use for**

- Expressing "off". Disabled and unpressed are different facts, and a disabled toggle can be either.

**Conflicts with** `loading`

**Accessibility** Emits `aria-disabled`, never the native `disabled` attribute: the control stays in the tab order and keeps announcing its pressed state.

### `loading`

```ts
loading?: boolean
```

Shows a spinner and refuses activation while the change this toggle asked for is still in flight.

Source doc: Shows a spinner and blocks activation while preserving focus.

**Use when**

- A toggle whose effect is a server round trip — starring, subscribing, publishing — where the state should not settle until the change lands.

**Don't use for**

- Flipping `pressed` optimistically *and* setting `loading`; pick one story about what the button currently means.
- Pairing it with `disabled` — `loading` already blocks activation, and the two together say the same thing twice.

**Conflicts with** `disabled`

**Accessibility** Emits `aria-busy` alongside `aria-disabled`, so the control is heard as busy rather than as broken. `aria-pressed` keeps reporting the state it is still in.

### `iconOnly`

```ts
iconOnly?: boolean
```

Square toggle carrying an icon and no visible text.

Source doc: Square icon-only toggle; pass the icon as children and set aria-label.

**Use when**

- Toolbars where the icons are conventional and the row would otherwise be unreadably wide — bold, italic, alignment.

**Don't use for**

- Icons whose meaning is not already settled. An unlabelled toggle with an ambiguous glyph is a control nobody can describe to a colleague.
- Relying on the icon alone to show the pressed state — the fill must change too.

**Accessibility** You MUST pass `aria-label`. Nothing supplies an accessible name when there is no visible text, and the name must stay constant across states — the state is `aria-pressed`'s job, not the label's.

## Use cases

### A formatting toggle in a toolbar

The canonical case: the state belongs to the document, so the toggle is controlled.

```tsx
<ToggleButton
  variant="tertiary"
  iconOnly
  aria-label="Bold"
  pressed={isBold}
  onPressedChange={setBold}
>
  B
</ToggleButton>
```

The label stays "Bold" in both states. `aria-pressed` says which state it is in — renaming it to "Unbold" would make the announcement contradict itself.

### A toggle whose change has to reach a server

Starring, subscribing, publishing — anything where the state should not settle until the write lands.

```tsx
<ToggleButton pressed={starred} loading={saving} onPressedChange={star}>
  Star
</ToggleButton>
```

`loading` blocks repeat activation on its own — don't also pass `disabled`. If the write fails, leave `pressed` where it was rather than flipping it back, which reads as the user having done something.

### Local-only state nothing else reads

The rare uncontrolled case: one view's own disclosure of extra detail.

```tsx
<ToggleButton defaultPressed onPressedChange={setShowDetail}>
  Show detail
</ToggleButton>
```

The moment a second place needs to know whether detail is showing, this becomes `pressed` — uncontrolled state that two components read is state that will disagree.

### Reaching for the wrong component

The control is a setting in a form, applied immediately, and reads as a thing with a state.

```tsx
<ToggleButton pressed={notifications} onPressedChange={setNotifications}>
  Notifications
</ToggleButton>
```

Don't. That is a switch, not a toggle button: it is a setting, not an action left engaged. Use Switch, which announces with aria-checked as "Notifications, on" — the sentence a setting should produce.

## Real usage in this repo

```tsx
<ToggleButton value="bold">Bold</ToggleButton>
```

## Token recipe

### secondary

The off state of a toggle that has to read as a control on its own — identical to the secondary button, because an unpressed toggle is one.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| background | `theme.secondary-role.bg` |
| color | `theme.secondary-role.fg` |
| border-color | `theme.secondary-role.border` |
| height | `size.control.md — and size.control.sm / .lg at the other sizes; this is the only thing `size` changes` |
| padding-inline | `space.control.padding-inline.md` |
| gap | `space.gap.xs` |
| border-radius | `radius.element` |
| font-size | `type.control.size.md — constant across all three sizes, so `size` changes the box and not the label` |
| font-weight | `type.control.weight` |
| line-height | `type.control.line-height.md — constant, as with font-size` |
| transition-duration | `motion.interactive.duration` |
| transition-timing-function | `motion.interactive.easing` |
| outline (focus-visible) | `focus.ring-width solid theme.focus-ring, offset focus.ring-offset` |
| hover/press | `compose the .rata-state-layer class — do not swap the background` |
| opacity (aria-disabled) | `state.disabled-opacity` |

### secondary-pressed

The on state: a tint, not a fill. A saturated accent background reads as "the action to take", which is the wrong sentence for "a state you are in" — the same reason this component has no primary variant.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| background | `theme.accent-role.subtle` |
| color | `theme.accent-role.fg` |
| border-color | `theme.accent-role.fg — the border moves with the fill, so the pressed state is not carried by background alone` |
| height | `size.control.md — and size.control.sm / .lg at the other sizes; this is the only thing `size` changes` |
| padding-inline | `space.control.padding-inline.md` |
| gap | `space.gap.xs` |
| border-radius | `radius.element` |
| font-size | `type.control.size.md — constant across all three sizes, so `size` changes the box and not the label` |
| font-weight | `type.control.weight` |
| line-height | `type.control.line-height.md — constant, as with font-size` |
| transition-duration | `motion.interactive.duration` |
| transition-timing-function | `motion.interactive.easing` |
| outline (focus-visible) | `focus.ring-width solid theme.focus-ring, offset focus.ring-offset` |
| hover/press | `compose the .rata-state-layer class — do not swap the background` |
| opacity (aria-disabled) | `state.disabled-opacity` |
